newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian oil officials head for Baghdad talks.
newsitem.headline: Russian oil officials head for Baghdad talks.

text.p: A Russian delegation headed by Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov left for Baghdad on Sunday for talks on economic topics including developing Iraqi oil reserves once U.N. sanctions are lifted, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Tass quoted Rodionov's deputy, Anatoly Shatalov, as saying talks on Tuesday and Wednesday would focus on the development of new deposits. Completing construction of oil plants and building new electric power stations were also on the agenda.
Russia's LUKoil is expected to sign a contract with Iraq to develop a prospective oil deposit, Western Qurna-2, whose oil reserves are estimated at one billion tonnes, Tass said.
The project is valued at $3.8 billion, the agency added.
Tass noted that Russia has long been eager to return to heavy economic cooperation with Iraq.

Another deputy energy minister Viktor Ott told reporters in London last week that Rodionov would head a delegation to Baghdad and said Russian oil executives accompanying the minister were hoping to sign contracts to develop Iraq's massive upstream potential, once United Nations sanctions are lifted.
